metadata.title: TIMSS 2011 Marcos de la evaluación
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center (Boston College) / IEA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a framework and assessment-design specification for TIMSS 2011 rather than an empirical analysis of student microdata. It describes the assessment structure (booklets, item blocks, test time, and context questionnaires) and the scaling approach used to place results on common TIMSS scales, but it does not report any student-level estimation procedure or the use of complex survey weights. For analysts working with TIMSS 2011 microdata, the intended design is a complex, clustered, multi-stage sample with booklet assignment, so population-representative inference typically requires applying TIMSS sampling weights and replicate weights as provided in the international database. However, because this text does not specify weight variable names or replicate methods, weight application details cannot be extracted from the framework itself.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/assessment-design publication that specifies content, cognitive domains, questionnaire coverage, and the test booklet design, but it does not estimate achievement models from student responses. As a result, plausible values handling and missing-data handling for an empirical achievement analysis are not part of the reported methodology in this document. Any PV or missing-data procedures would be implemented in the subsequent TIMSS technical/scaling reports and international scoring pipeline rather than in this assessment framework.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used as an assessment framework for TIMSS 2011; no analytic student sample is defined or analyzed in this document. It specifies target populations by grade/ISCED level and provides design targets (e.g., test time, booklet structure, and questionnaire administration), but does not report an empirical dataset extraction or inclusion/exclusion rules.

data.outcome_summary: This publication provides the theoretical frameworks and evaluation specifications for TIMSS 2011 mathematics and science, covering two target grades: 4th grade of primary education (about 10 years) and 2nd grade of lower secondary/ESO (about 14 years). It defines the content domains (e.g., numbers, algebra, geometry, data and probability; life science, physical science, earth science) and the cognitive domains (knowing, applying, reasoning), including target proportions of test time across domains. The assessment design uses a matrix sampling approach: items are organized into 28 item blocks per subject, distributed across 14 student booklets, with each student completing one booklet and receiving a context questionnaire. Performance reporting is based on scaling to common TIMSS metrics (international mean 500, SD 100) and domain-specific scales, enabling trend comparisons across cycles. The document does not present empirical model results or predictive analytics; it is intended to guide item development, scoring procedures, and the interpretation structure for later TIMSS reporting.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a non-empirical assessment framework rather than an empirical study. Consequently, there is no analytic student sample, no country-level sample sizes, no missing-data or PV estimation strategy for an achievement model, and no ML training/evaluation pipeline reported. The sparse fields (e.g., empty countries, null sample size, no findings) reflect the document’s purpose: to specify what TIMSS 2011 measures and how the test is constructed and scaled, not to estimate effects or predictive performance.
